title: What SS5/25 Means for Insurers: Lessons From Climate Adaptation for Managing Deep Uncertainty
content:
ABSTRACT

In 2015, Mark Carney, the then Governor of the Bank of England (BoE), gave a speech at Lloyd's of London titled ‘Breaking the tragedy of the horizon—climate change and financial stability’. It was a call to action, highlighting the importance of recognising risks that climate change poses to the financial sector and services, whilst noting the obvious challenges caused by the mismatch in time horizons of climate impacts versus business cycles and perceived business relevance. In years that followed, policy language on climate risk from BoE and international counterparts has evolved from awareness-raising and encouraging capacity building to explicit implementation. The latest BoE supervisory statement (SS5/25; December 2025) marks a step change with enhanced expectations on governance, understanding of data, scenario analysis and embedding climate risk in existing risk frameworks: a move towards treating climate risk as a core prudential risk. In this perspective, we consider the requirements of the SS5/25. We discuss why forward-looking risk assessment poses a challenge to a sector that prides itself on its ability to quantify and price risk, and suggest how practitioners can learn from perspectives and approaches applied in climate adaptation communities that manage risk under deep uncertainty.
